title: introduce-reservoir-headroom-with-momentum-and-soft-fallbacks
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Adds a reservoir-based headroom allocator with tenant momentum smoothing, opt-in via feature flag. Improves throughput stability under bursty load and provides new telemetry for per-tenant headroom, momentum, and fallback events.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated capacity customers see transient microbursts that either overcommit warm pools or cause reactive autoscaler thrash. Current heuristics (fixed headroom + simple moving averages) either under-provision or overspend during sustained ramp-ups. This change introduces a reservoir-based headroom allocator that maintains a decayed credit reservoir per tenant and a small "momentum" factor to bias short-term headroom growth while preserving long-term fairness and cost controls.

Design summary: the allocator keeps a time-decayed reservoir (float) for each tenant representing available soft headroom. Incoming utilization impulses either replenish or draw from the reservoir. A momentum multiplier boosts allocation when recent utilization is trending upward, enabling smoother warm-pool prewarming without aggressive cluster-wide provisioning. When reservoir is depleted, the system falls back to a configurable soft-fallback policy that prefers: 1) local warmpool borrow, 2) cross-pool temporary loan, 3) negotiated degrade path (lower concurrency or quantized model variant). All behaviors are policy-driven via a new dedicated autoscaler config object.

Key changes: - pkg/autoscaler/reservoir_allocator.go: new allocator implementation, reservoir decay loop, concurrency-safe token accounting. - pkg/autoscaler/policy.go: adds momentum factor, fallback priority resolver, and circuit state machine for depletion events. - pkg/telemetry/headroom_metrics.go: new metrics (headroom_reservoir_{tenant}, headroom_momentum_factor, fallback_trigger_count, fallback_path). - configs/dedicated/autoscaler.yaml: new policy knobs and defaults (decay_tau, momentum_window, soft_fallback_order). - internal/e2e/dedicated_reservoir_test.go: synthetic burst scenarios, regression guards. - docs/dedicated/reservoir-headroom.md: design doc + rollout guidance + knob matrix.

Compatibility & rollout: feature-gated behind `reservoir_headroom_v1` and defaulted to off for existing Dedicated clusters. We will enable in canary (one dedicated pool) for 48h synthetic traffic then promote gradually if no regressions. Configuration is backward-compatible: when the feature flag is off, the previous fixed-headroom allocator path is used.

Telemetry & observability: new per-tenant metrics enable post-rollout analysis: - headroom_reservoir_bytes (gauge) - headroom_momentum (gauge, 0.0-3.0) - headroom_fallback_total (counter with labels path=local|crosspool|degrade) - headroom_reservoir_fill_rate (histogram) We added dashboards and an alert (HighFallbackRate) to detect unexpected depletion patterns.

Performance: microbenchmarks on a 32-GPU dev cluster with synthetic bursts (50 tenants, Poisson spikes) show: - 22% reduction in provisioning churn (measured as warm-pool resize ops/sec) - 9% lower 95th latency for short bursts (p95 token latency) - <1% median overhead on steady-state scheduling path. All numbers from lab runs are included in docs/dedicated/benchmarks.md.

Security & cost: no customer data is persisted beyond tenant identifiers for telemetry. Cost impact controlled via conservative defaults; operators can tune decay_tau and momentum_window to trade latency vs cost.

Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature in canary dedicated pool (QA) 2) Monitor HighFallbackRate and warmpool resize charts for 48h 3) Gradually enable on 10% of dedicated capacity for 1 week 4) Full rollout after SRE sign-off.

Notes: This PR purposely separates policy from allocator internals to make future strategy experimentation (RL-based replenishment, ML forecasts) easier. Related: ENG-4821 (autoscale stability), SUP-9142 (customer reported thrash during Black Friday test).
